provision_review.why: Pensions Act 2014 s.3 sets the reduced rate at 1/35 of the full rate per qualifying year, and the eligibility page sets a 10-year minimum. The pre-fix new-pension rule instead prorates a reported data-year receipt and never uses qualifying years. provision.txt alone gives only the 35-year full-rate condition, not the proportional formula or the minimum.

triage.pre_fix_wrong_because: The pre-fix module derived the state pension from a reported dataset-year receipt prorated by dataset-year rate ceilings and then scaled by policy levers (`state_pension_abolished_by_policy`, `state_pension_policy_uprating_factor`) that appear nowhere in the uprating order it cited, instead of the qualifying-years proportion the source sets out (1/35 of the full new state pension, with no entitlement below 10 qualifying years; 30 years for the full basic pension).
triage.triage_notes: Provision read: the vendored slice uk/statute/ukpga/2014/19/3 says "The reduced rate of the state pension for a person is the following proportion of the full rate— 1/35 × the person's number of qualifying years", and the gov.uk slices supply the 35-year full rate, 10-year minimum and 30-year basic full rate - so the post-fix formulas are grounded and the pre-fix prorating / abolition / uprating-factor branches were not. This is the clearest untraceable_branch instance in the chunk and the one the commit message names most specifically ("state pension from qualifying years"). Also fixes the timeline: version windows move from a single 2026-04-06 window to 2016-04-06 (new) and 2010-04-06 (basic), and the additional/protected state pension amount above the ceiling is dropped entirely (additional state pension is no longer encoded - a coverage loss a reviewer may want to note). New rule uses min(1, years/35) so records above 35 qualifying years cap at the full rate.
triage.verifier_justification: The pre-fix module declared `source_verification.corpus_citation_path: uk/regulation/uksi/2026/148/article/4` and carried a `kind: formula` proof atom asserting its formula was supported by that provision, but resolving that citation through the pinned release returns only a rate substitution ("In section 44(4) of the Contributions and Benefits Act ... for \"£176.45\" substitute \"£184.90\""), which says nothing about dataset-year receipt proration, an abolition switch, or a policy uprating multiplier. The three surfaces were therefore formulas grounded on the wrong provision, with two branches (`state_pension_abolished_by_policy`, `state_pension_policy_uprating_factor`) having no basis in any cited source, which is the untraceable_branch definition including "formulas grounded on the wrong provision." The fix removes them and re-grounds on Pensions Act 2014 s.3, whose resolved text ("The reduced rate of the state pension for a person is the following proportion of the full rate— 1/35 × the person's number of qualifying years") matches the new formula. The "this was deliberate scaffolding, not an error" refutation fails because the module ran with `proof_validation: required: true` and affirmatively cited article 4 as the formula's source; the maintainer's own words confirm the pattern was debt, not design ("those surfaces are the old pattern this PR removes ... `reported_*` inputs").
triage.verifier_notes: Refutation attempts and why they failed: (1) "mechanical" is untenable — formulas, rule names, effective dates and the output set all changed. (2) "not_a_defect / enhancement" is the strongest counter-reading, since the pre-fix summary openly said "This PolicyEngine-alignment surface returns the weekly State Pension amount used by PolicyEngine UK", i.e. it was a knowingly-labeled model wrapper rather than a misread of law, and the PR title frames it as "PolicyEngine wrapper retirement." It fails only because the module simultaneously asserted source grounding it did not have: proof atom `corpus_citation_path: uk/regulation/uksi/2026/148/article/4` / `excerpt: "Category A basic retirement pension"` on a formula that proration and policy levers cannot be derived from. If the taxonomy treats a self-declared alignment wrapper as "never claimed" law fidelity, this would drop to unclear — that is the one reviewer judgment call here. (3) Competing kinds: the fix also moves effective_from 2026-04-06 → 2016-04-06 / 2010-04-06 (wrong_period_or_effective_date), drops the `current_state_pension_flat_weekly_amount` and `additional_state_pension_weekly_amount` outputs (wrong_entity_or_scope), and adds the 10-year floor and 35/30-year proportions (unrepresented_clause). All three are consequences of the re-grounding rather than the primary defect, so untraceable_branch remains the best single fit. Provenance caveats for the reviewer: the guidance slices were captured by hand on 2026-06-10, not through the corpus extractor, and the corpus resolver reports `fix_time_corpus_match: provision_file_absent_at_corpus_ref` with `selection_basis: earliest_release_after_toolchain_corpus_ref`, so both source texts were read from release uk-rulespec-2026-07-12 rather than the exact fix-time corpus. Also note the commit was hand-authored, not encoder-produced ("Ah I see I should have got the encoder to do this rather than claude... will refile"), which bears on the repo's encoding regime but not on the fidelity classification. Finally, the post-fix encoding is guidance-level and omits transitional starting-amount / protected-payment rules — a simplification, but not evidence against the pre-fix defect.
